facts.fact_text: The applicants and some other people (several dozen in total) disagreed with the course of action of demolishing Voronezh municipal market and building a shopping centre, which would adversely affect their businesses and employment.
The applicants and some other people (several dozen in total) decided to remain on the Voronezh municipal market premises permanently, doing 'night shifts'.

According to the applicants, on an unspecified date and in a specified manner, the entrepreneurs notified the town administration of their intention to 'constantly do night shifts at the market until the matters relating to the legality of the land's transfer and the demolition of the market were settled'.
The entrepreneurs started their 'night shifts' at Voronezh municipal market on an unspecified date.
On 6 August 2009 the police told the entrepreneurs who had gathered at Voronezh municipal market to leave the premises.
Some entrepreneurs refused to comply with the police order to leave Voronezh municipal market premises in the absence of any court order.
Some entrepreneurs argued that, under their rent contracts, they had a right to remain at Voronezh municipal market.
On 6 August 2009 the police told the entrepreneurs who had gathered at Voronezh municipal market to leave the premises.
Some entrepreneurs refused to comply with the police order to leave Voronezh municipal market premises in the absence of any court order.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Annenkov was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Khripunov was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Khavantsev was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Finskiy was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Ms Suprunova was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Ms Zakharova was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Ms Guseva was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
By a judgment of 7 August 2009 a justice of the peace convicted Mr Finskiy of an offence under Article 19.3 of the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO).
The justice of the peace sentenced Mr Finskiy to five days' administrative detention by judgment of 7 August 2009.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Khripunov was sentenced to five days' administrative detention by a justice of the peace.
Mr Khavantsev was sentenced to ten days' administrative detention.

As required under the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO), Mr Finskiy, Mr Khavantsev and Mr Khripunov started to serve their sentences of administrative detention immediately following the trial judgments in their cases.
At 5.30 a.m. on 10 August 2009 the police arrested some twenty people at Voronezh municipal market.
Among those arrested at 5.30 a.m. on 10 August 2009 at Voronezh municipal market were applicants Mr Buzov, Ms Garkavets, Ms Zhuravleva, Ms Khavantseva and Ms Suprunova.
By a judgment of 10 August 2009 Mr Buzov was convicted of an offence under Article 19.3 of the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO).
Mr Buzov was sentenced to ten days' administrative detention by the justice of the peace by judgment of 10 August 2009.
According to the Government, Mr Buzov did not serve his sentence of ten days' administrative detention, as he was taken to the cardiology unit of a local hospital on the evening of 10 August 2009.

At the material time, Article 19.3 § 1 of the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO) punished with a fine or administrative detention the following behaviour: disobeying the lawful order of a police officer, a military officer or a detention facility staff member in relation to the fulfilment of their official duties aimed at securing public order and public safety.

At the material time, Article 19.3 § 1 of the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO) also punished with a fine or administrative detention resisting the fulfilment of such duties by police officers, military officers or detention facility staff members.

The Police Act 1991 (Federal Law no. 1026-I of 18 April 1991) authorised police officers to use physical force, including combat fighting techniques, to stop crimes being committed, apprehend offenders, and overcome resistance to lawful orders, if less intrusive means had not allowed the officers to fulfil their functions (section 13 of the Police Act 1991).

Under the Police Act 1991 (Federal Law no. 1026-I of 18 April 1991), everyone was required to comply with the lawful order of a police officer, and failure to comply with such an order, or obstruction in relation to such an order, would result in the person concerned incurring legal liability.
The justice of the peace held that Mr Finskiy disobeyed a lawful order issued by police officers in relation to their duties to ensure public order and safety.
The justice of the peace held that Mr Finskiy obstructed police officers' exercise of their duties to ensure public order and safety.
The justice of the peace held that Mr Khripunov disobeyed a lawful order issued by police officers in relation to their duties to ensure public order and safety.
The justice of the peace held that Mr Khripunov obstructed police officers' exercise of their duties to ensure public order and safety.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh dismissed the argument that the police had acted unlawfully in relation to the entrepreneurs' presence at a gathering requiring no prior authorisation, finding that the police had acted lawfully with the aim of ensuring public order and public safety because the entrepreneurs were blocking access to the market for employees and had not reacted to lawful orders from the police to stop these actions.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh dismissed the defence's argument that Mr Khripunov had lawfully participated in a gathering requiring no prior authorisation, finding that the police's actions were lawful and aimed to secure public order and public safety since the entrepreneurs were blocking the market employees' access to the building.

The Deputy President of the Voronezh Regional Court held that Mr Buzov was part of the group of people who impeded market officials as they tried to gain access to their office building, that guards from a private security company intervened and a fight ensued between them and some participants, that these participants did not respond to orders from police officers, and that the officers required Mr Buzov, who was one of the most active participants, to cease his unlawful conduct, but he did not respond to this order, and was thereafter taken to the police station.

Mr Finskiy, Mr Khavantsev and Mr Khripunov were accused of an offence under Article 19.3 of the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO), which punished disobeying or resisting the lawful order of a public official.

Mr Finskiy, Mr Khavantsev and Mr Khripunov denied that they had disobeyed or resisted any specific lawful orders from the police, or that they had otherwise breached the public order or endangered public safety.

A witness identified as N. stated before the justice of the peace that on 7 August 2009 a group of entrepreneurs were doing night shifts to prevent the demolition of the market building, that police officers arrived and started to grab people and take them to the police station, and that Mr Khripunov was grabbed by the police but did not show any resistance during this procedure.

The justice of the peace adopted a critical stance in relation to the testimony of witness N., who was Mr Khripunov's acquaintance and colleague, because this testimony was refuted by the bulk of the other evidence, namely the officers' written reports made in their official capacity.

Mr Khripunov and Mr Finskiy argued before the Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh that they had taken part in a 'gathering', and the Federal Law on Gatherings, Meetings, Demonstrations, Processions and Pickets (the Public Events Act) did not require that prior notice be given to the competent public authority for this type of public event.

Mr Khripunov and Mr Finskiy argued before the Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh that, in breach of the Federal Law on Gatherings, Meetings, Demonstrations, Processions and Pickets (the Public Events Act), no written requirement to cease any unlawful conduct had been issued to them or the other entrepreneurs.

Witnesses B., Ma. and L. stated that while passing through Voronezh municipal market on the morning of 7 August 2009, they had seen a group of some fifty people shouting slogans and calling for people in the town and regional administrations to be dismissed, as well as calling for the violation of public order.
Witnesses B., Ma. and L. stated that the police had told the group of people to stop, but they had not complied with that order.

Witnesses B., Ma. and L. stated that the police had repeated the warning to the most active participant, and after he had failed to comply, he had been taken to a police car while grabbing the officers' uniforms and trying to run away.

Officers S., Y. and F. submitted written reports stating that on 6 August 2009, noting the blocking of the entrance to the office building at Voronezh municipal market, they had ordered the people present to disperse.
Officers S., Y. and F. submitted written reports stating that on 7 August 2009 they again ordered the people present at Voronezh municipal market to disperse.

Officers S., Y. and F. submitted written reports stating that approaching Mr Finskiy, whom they identified as one of the most active participants, they had ordered him to stop, and after he had refused, they had taken him to the police station.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh heard Ms D. in the appeal proceedings, who stated that Mr Finskiy had been trying to film the ongoing events when the police had taken him away and that he had not shown any resistance.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh stated it had no reason to doubt the testimonies of police officers and witnesses L., B. and Ma. because they were not previously acquainted with Mr Finskiy or other entrepreneurs and had no reason to give false testimony against him.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh dismissed the argument that witnesses L., B. and Ma. could not be eyewitnesses since the market was surrounded by a wall, finding that their testimonies indicated they had effectively passed through the marketplace.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh dismissed the argument that the police had acted unlawfully in relation to the entrepreneurs' presence at a gathering requiring no prior authorisation, finding that the police had acted lawfully with the aim of ensuring public order and public safety because the entrepreneurs were blocking access to the market for employees and had not reacted to lawful orders from the police to stop these actions.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh adopted a critical attitude in respect of the testimony of Ms D., finding that she had tried to help her colleague Mr Finskiy avoid responsibility for the offence and that her testimony was refuted by the other evidence.

Witness P. stated before the Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh that on 7 August 2009 people in plain clothes and the police arrived at Voronezh municipal market and, following orders from the chief officer of the Sovetskiy police station, started to arrest entrepreneurs without explaining the reasons for such arrests, and that Mr Khripunov was arrested while showing no resistance or disobedience to any specific orders.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh found that the record of the administrative offence against Mr Khripunov stated that after his violation of the procedure for organising and managing public events, while being arrested, he disobeyed the lawful order of a police officer, grabbed his uniform and tried to escape.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh found that written statements from three passers-by confirmed that some fifty people were chanting slogans and calling for the dismissal of the mayor and the governor and for violations of the public order, that despite the police's order to stop, the entrepreneurs refused, and that Mr Khripunov, who appeared particularly active, did not respond to a further order to stop, resisted while being placed in the police car, and threatened the officers with violence and prosecution.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh found that officers' written statements confirmed that having approached Mr Khripunov as one of the most active men, they warned him against committing offences but he did not react and refused to stop, and was thus arrested and taken to the police station (the officers' reports mistakenly referred to him as 'Finskiy').

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh dismissed the defence's argument that Mr Khripunov had lawfully participated in a gathering requiring no prior authorisation, finding that the police's actions were lawful and aimed to secure public order and public safety since the entrepreneurs were blocking the market employees' access to the building.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh adopted a critical attitude in respect of the testimony of witness P., who was Mr Khripunov's colleague, finding that P.'s testimony was refuted by the bulk of the other evidence.
In late September 2009 Mr Finskiy, Mr Khavantsev and Mr Khripunov learnt that court decisions in respect of certain other participants in the same events had been quashed on appeal in September 2009.

On 8 October 2009 Mr Finskiy, Mr Khavantsev and Mr Khripunov lodged applications under Article 30.12 of the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO) for review of the final judgments in respect of them.
On 20 November 2009 the Deputy President of the Voronezh Regional Court upheld the lower courts' decisions in respect of Mr Finskiy, Mr Khavantsev and Mr Khripunov.

The Deputy President of the Voronezh Regional Court dismissed the defence's argument that the lower courts' judges had omitted to specify the type of public event in which the defendants had participated, the relevant regulations on such public events, and the specific details concerning the police's orders to the defendants, stating that it had been established by the justice of the peace that the impugned event was a 'gathering'.
By judgments of 7 August 2009 the female defendants in the proceedings (Ms Suprunova, Ms Zakharova and Ms Guseva) and Mr Annenkov were fined.
On 2 September 2009 the Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh set aside the judgment of 7 August 2009 in respect of Mr Annenkov.
On 8 September 2009 the Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh set aside the judgment of 7 August 2009 in respect of one or more of the female defendants.
On 10 September 2009 the Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh set aside the judgment of 7 August 2009 in respect of one or more of the female defendants.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held in respect of Mr Annenkov that neither the record of the administrative offence nor the judgment contained references to specific circumstances or actions relating to the corpus delicti of the imputed offence of disobeying the lawful order of a police officer, and in particular neither document specified what order was given to Mr Annenkov which was then not complied with, and the judgment did not indicate that Mr Annenkov had disobeyed a lawful order issued by a police officer.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held in respect of Ms Guseva that the record of the administrative offence did not specify what type of public event was being held, which procedure was violated, or what orders relating to maintaining public order during a public event were not complied with by Ms Guseva.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held in respect of Ms Suprunova that the record of the administrative offence did not indicate what type of public event was being held, which applicable procedure Ms Suprunova allegedly violated, what orders relating to maintaining public order during such an event were issued to Ms Suprunova by the police, or which of those orders was not complied with.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held in respect of Ms Zakharova that neither the record of the administrative offence nor the first-instance judgment referred to specific facts and actions forming part of the offence imputed to Ms Zakharova of disobeying the lawful order of a police officer, or the specific order given to her which she failed to comply with, and the record did not specify what Ms Zakharova's violation of the procedure concerning the organisation and management of demonstrations, meetings and gatherings was, or what type of event was being held.
The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh ordered the return of the case files concerning Mr Annenkov, Ms Suprunova, Ms Zakharova and Ms Guseva to the relevant justice of the peace.

The justice of the peace returned the case files concerning Mr Annenkov, Ms Suprunova, Ms Zakharova and Ms Guseva to the police station, apparently for the documents to be amended or the administrative-offence records to be redrafted.
The case files concerning Mr Annenkov, Ms Suprunova, Ms Zakharova and Ms Guseva were not resubmitted for a retrial.

The justice of the peace heard Ms Khr., who stated that a group of people had impeded security guards as they tried to re-establish access to the market building, and that the police had then arrived and had taken some people to the police station.
During the hearing before the justice of the peace on 10 August 2009, Mr Buzov, who was assisted by counsel, first sought to have some other witnesses and police officers examined in open court.
According to the Government, Mr Buzov then withdrew his application to have other witnesses and police officers examined in open court.
The justice of the peace found that Mr Buzov disobeyed the police officers and did not comply with lawful orders to stop violating public order.
The justice of the peace found that Mr Buzov's guilt was confirmed by the administrative-offence record, the police officers' reports and the written testimonies of witnesses.
Mr Buzov appealed to the Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh against his conviction of 10 August 2009.
The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held a hearing on 13 August 2009 in respect of Mr Buzov's appeal.
The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh heard Mr Buzov's lawyer at the hearing on 13 August 2009.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh heard Ms Yef. at the hearing on 13 August 2009, who stated that she had seen Mr Buzov making a video recording while surrounded by security guards who had torn his clothes, that colleagues had managed to get him out of the security guards' grasp, that the police had then arrived and started to push certain entrepreneurs aside, that one of the security guards had given an order to arrest Mr Buzov, and that Mr Buzov had not disobeyed any orders and had not resisted arrest.
By a decision of 13 August 2009 the Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh upheld the judgment of 10 August 2009 in respect of Mr Buzov.

In late September 2009 Mr Buzov and his counsel Ms Gnezdilova learnt that court decisions in respect of certain other participants in the events on 10 August 2009 and 7 August 2009 had been quashed on appeal.
Mr Buzov and his counsel Ms Gnezdilova thought they had a reasonable prospect of success in seeking a further review of the court decisions of 10 and 13 August 2009.
In early October 2009 Mr Buzov and his counsel Ms Gnezdilova lodged an application for review of the court decisions of 10 and 13 August 2009.

Mr Buzov and his counsel Ms Gnezdilova argued in their application for review that the lower courts had not specified what specific order Mr Buzov had disobeyed or whether such an order was lawful under Russian law.

Mr Buzov and his counsel Ms Gnezdilova argued in their application for review that the courts had not heard any officers or eyewitnesses who had witnessed the impugned reprehensible conduct on the part of Mr Buzov.
Mr Buzov and his counsel Ms Gnezdilova argued in their application for review that the courts had not specified any particular actions on Mr Buzov's part which constituted a breach of public order.
On 20 November 2009 the Deputy President of the Voronezh Regional Court upheld the lower courts' decisions in respect of Mr Buzov.

The Deputy President of the Voronezh Regional Court held that Mr Buzov was part of the group of people who impeded market officials as they tried to gain access to their office building, that guards from a private security company intervened and a fight ensued between them and some participants, that these participants did not respond to orders from police officers, and that the officers required Mr Buzov, who was one of the most active participants, to cease his unlawful conduct, but he did not respond to this order, and was thereafter taken to the police station.
On 10 August 2009 a justice of the peace sentenced several female defendants (Ms Garkavets, Ms Zhuravleva and Ms Khavantseva) to a fine.
On 8 September 2009 the Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh heard appeals from the female defendants sentenced on 10 August 2009 and set aside the judgments against them.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held in respect of Ms Zhuravleva that the record of the administrative offence did not specify which requests relating to public order were addressed to Ms Zhuravleva and were not complied with, or which actions of Ms Zhuravleva such requests related to, and that the deficiencies of the record made it impossible to establish Ms Zhuravleva's liability for an administrative offence, and the record must be returned to the police.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held in respect of Ms Khavantseva and Ms Garkavets that neither the record of the administrative offence nor the justice of the peace's judgment specified how each defendant violated public order, or which specific order was given by the police in this connection but not complied with by her.
The case files concerning the female defendants sentenced on 10 August 2009 were returned to the police for the documents to be amended.
The case files concerning the female defendants sentenced on 10 August 2009 were not resubmitted to the relevant justice of the peace for a retrial.

Unspecified officials carried out an inquiry between 10 and 18 August 2009 into whether any police officers had committed the offence of abuse of power under Article 286 of the Criminal Code, defined at the time as 'actions manifestly outside the scope of official duties, causing a significant violation of one's rights or legitimate interests'.

On 19 August 2009 an investigator issued a decision refusing to institute criminal proceedings against police officers, referring to the statements of several officers including Officer Ku., and the testimonies of Mr Annenkov, Ms Shatalova, Ms Zakharova and Ms Suprunova.
The refusal to institute criminal proceedings issued on 19 August 2009 was overruled for unspecified reasons and the inquiry was resumed.
Written statements were obtained from some other participants in the gathering at Voronezh municipal market as part of the resumed inquiry.
Officer Kh. was heard during the resumed inquiry and confirmed Officer Ku.'s earlier statement.
On 7 September 2009 the investigator issued a new refusal to institute criminal proceedings against Officer Ku., Officer Kh. or other officers.
The investigator concluded on 7 September 2009 that no sufficient and objective data could be gathered during the inquiry to show that any police officers had committed any criminal offence.
The investigator concluded on 7 September 2009 that the grievances presented in the complaints were refuted by the testimonies from the officers.

The investigator concluded on 7 September 2009 that injuries could have been sustained during the arrest procedure owing to the resistance displayed to the police officers, such resistance later being confirmed by the prosecution for the administrative offences.

The investigator concluded on 7 September 2009 that in view of the important and irremediable inconsistencies in various testimonies, there was no possibility of drawing a truthful conclusion regarding the commission of a criminal offence by Officer Ku., Officer Kh. or others.
A new refusal to prosecute was issued on 1 October 2009 for unspecified reasons.
The refusal to prosecute of 1 October 2009 was overruled on 7 October 2009 by the deputy director of the District Investigations Department.

The deputy director of the District Investigations Department indicated on 7 October 2009 that it was necessary to assess the available court decisions regarding administrative offences concerning the events on 7 August 2009.

The deputy director of the District Investigations Department indicated on 7 October 2009 that it was necessary to identify and interview people who had been kept with the arrested people at the police station.

The deputy director of the District Investigations Department indicated on 7 October 2009 that it was necessary to identify and interview all police officers who had been present at the station and had compiled administrative-offence files against the arrested entrepreneurs.

The deputy director of the District Investigations Department indicated on 7 October 2009 that it was necessary to identify and interview all the officers who had been on duty on 7 August 2009 and had been present at Voronezh municipal market.
Four applicants (Mr Annenkov, Ms Suprunova, Ms Guseva and Ms Zakharova) sought judicial review in respect of the refusal to prosecute dated 1 October 2009.
At a hearing on 19 October 2009, Mr Annenkov, Ms Suprunova, Ms Guseva and Ms Zakharova learnt that the refusal to prosecute of 1 October 2009 had already been overruled.
The judicial review case brought by Mr Annenkov, Ms Suprunova, Ms Guseva and Ms Zakharova in respect of the refusal to prosecute of 1 October 2009 was discontinued.
A new refusal to prosecute was issued on 9 November 2009.
On 22 December 2009 the Regional Investigations Department set aside the refusal to prosecute of 9 November 2009.

The Regional Investigations Department set aside the refusal of 9 November 2009 because it contained an insufficient assessment of the factual circumstances, no plausible explanation for the applicants' injuries, and no assessment of the legality of the police's actions.
Being unaware of the Regional Investigations Department's decision of 22 December 2009, one of the applicants sought judicial review of the refusal to prosecute dated 9 November 2009.

On 9 November 2010 the Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh discontinued the judicial review proceedings concerning the refusal to prosecute of 9 November 2009 because the supervising authority had overruled the impugned refusal decision.
According to the Government, a new refusal to prosecute was issued on 19 June 2012.
The refusal to prosecute of 19 June 2012 was overruled on 5 October 2012 by the district prosecutor's office.
After the refusal to prosecute of 19 June 2012 was overruled, a criminal case was opened under Article 286 of the Criminal Code.
Apparently, Mr Annenkov and Ms Suprunova at least were interviewed again by an investigator following the opening of the criminal case under Article 286 of the Criminal Code.
Mr Annenkov had a formal confrontation procedure with an unspecified witness who had allegedly seen Mr Annenkov stumble and fall to the ground by himself on 7 August 2009.
